chart.title: Comparatives with -er
rows: Leo is taller than his friend.
A cheetah is faster than a horse.
My sister is older than me.
A mouse is smaller than a cat.
chart.note: Add -er to short adjectives (1 syllable). If the adjective ends in -e, just add -r. If it ends in consonant+vowel+consonant, double the last consonant.

sentences: Leo is taller than his friend.
A cheetah is faster than a horse.
This book is older than that one.
My bag is heavier than yours.
This road is longer than that one.
My phone is newer than my dad's.
The soup is thicker than the juice.
That mountain is higher than this one.

rules.title: Short adjectives (1 syllable) → add -er
rules.explanation: For most short adjectives, simply add -er. tall → taller, fast → faster, cold → colder.
examples: Leo is taller than his friend.

rules.title: Adjectives ending in -e → add -r only
rules.explanation: When the adjective already ends in -e, just add -r. nice → nicer, large → larger.
examples: This room is nicer than that one.

rules.title: CVC adjectives → double the consonant, add -er
rules.explanation: If the adjective has one syllable and ends in consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC), double the final consonant. big → bigger, hot → hotter, thin → thinner.
examples: An elephant is bigger than a horse.

rules.title: Use 'than' after the comparative
rules.explanation: Always use 'than' to connect what you are comparing. Never use 'then' here.
examples: English is easier than Chinese for Leo.

rules.title: Long adjectives (2+ syllables) → use 'more', not -er
rules.explanation: For longer adjectives, don't add -er. Use 'more' before the adjective instead. beautiful → more beautiful. This is covered in Grammar 2.
examples: This film is more interesting than that one.
Science is more difficult than art.

quiz.question: Leo is _____ than his classmate. (tall)
quiz.explanation: Short adjectives add -er. tall → taller. We never say 'more tall' for short adjectives.

quiz.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Tokyo is more big than Osaka.
Tokyo is most big than Osaka.
quiz.explanation: big → bigger (CVC rule: double the g). Use 'than', not 'then'.

quiz.question: My bag is _____ than yours. (heavy)
quiz.explanation: heavy ends in consonant+y → change y to i, add -er → heavier.

quiz.question: Which word completes: 'This road is longer _____ that one.'
quiz.explanation: Always use 'than' after a comparative adjective — never 'then'.

quiz.question: nice → ?
quiz.explanation: nice ends in -e, so just add -r → nicer.

quiz.question: hot → ?
quiz.explanation: hot is CVC (h-o-t) → double the t → hotter.

quiz.question: A cheetah is _____ than a horse. (fast)
quiz.explanation: fast is a short adjective → faster. Simple -er rule.

quiz.question: Which is NOT a comparative form?
quiz.explanation: beautiful has 3 syllables — we use 'more beautiful', never 'beautifuler'.

quiz.question: My sister is _____ than me. (old)
quiz.explanation: old → older. Standard short adjective rule.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Today is _____ yesterday.' (cold)
quiz.explanation: cold → colder. Always followed by 'than' when making a comparison.

master_quiz.question: A mouse is _____ than a cat.
Which uses 'than' correctly?
options: She is more tall than him.
